commit.message:
fix: preserve original_order when updating a transaction

Every transaction touched by `update_transactions` came back with
`original_order = NULL`. NULL sorts last, so on the next `sync up` those
rows were written at the very bottom of the Transactions tab, below the
oldest row, regardless of date.

`get_transaction_impl` omitted `original_order` from its SELECT and filled
the field via `..Default::default()`, which produced `None`.
`update_transaction_impl` then wrote every column back, binding that `None`
as NULL. The fetch was incomplete but the write was complete.

The SELECT now includes the column. The struct literal also lists every
remaining field explicitly instead of falling back on
`..Default::default()`, so a field added to `Transaction` in the future is
a compile error here rather than a silent NULL. The one field with no
column to read from, `no_name`, is set explicitly with a comment saying so.

The category and autocat getters already listed their fields explicitly,
which is why only transactions were affected.

Fixes #40

files.patch:
@@ -14,6 +14,8 @@ adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
 - `--other-field` on the `insert` and `update` subcommands is now optional and no longer panics when
   supplied. Repeating it adds one custom column per occurrence. [#41]
 - Negative amounts can now be given as `--amount -12.34` instead of only `--amount=-12.34`.
+- Updating a transaction no longer clears its `original_order`, which had caused updated rows to be
+  written to the bottom of the Transactions tab on the next `sync up`. [#40]
 
 ### Changed
 
@@ -96,4 +98,5 @@ adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
 [#24]: https://github.com/webern/tiller-sync/issues/24
 [#28]: https://github.com/webern/tiller-sync/issues/28
 [#36]: https://github.com/webern/tiller-sync/issues/36
+[#40]: https://github.com/webern/tiller-sync/issues/40
 [#41]: https://github.com/webern/tiller-sync/issues/41

@@ -606,7 +606,7 @@ impl Db {
                 transaction_id, date, description, amount, account, account_number,
                 institution, month, week, full_description, account_id, check_number,
                 date_added, merchant_name, category_hint, category, note, tags,
-                categorized_date, statement, metadata, other_fields
+                categorized_date, statement, metadata, other_fields, original_order
             FROM transactions WHERE transaction_id = ?"#,
         )
         .bind(id)
@@ -663,7 +663,10 @@ impl Db {
                     statement: r.get::<Option<String>, _>("statement").unwrap_or_default(),
                     metadata: r.get::<Option<String>, _>("metadata").unwrap_or_default(),
                     other_fields,
-                    ..Default::default()
+                    original_order: r.get::<Option<u64>, _>("original_order"),
+                    // `no_name` (the unnamed column A that some sheets have) has no column in the
+                    // `transactions` table, so there is nothing to read it from.
+                    no_name: String::new(),
                 }))
             }
         }
